This is a petition filed under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Anjinappa in a road traffic accident.
claiming for compensation of with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 2.

The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 15.09.2018, the deceased Anjinappa H.K., after attending the marriage at H.Cross along with his villager by name Narayanappa and Bharath Kumar were returning back to their house in a Omni Car bearing Reg.No.KA40M1885, which was driven by deceased Anjinappa.H.K. on the extreme left side of the road slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations and while so proceeding at about 9.30 p.m., reached in between DevanahalliGambeeranahalli village.

At that time, suddenly the driver of Wagon R car bearing Reg.No.KA04MK5988 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and came to his extreme right and dashed against Omni car bearing Reg.No.KA40M1885 and due to the terrific impact, deceased and other inmates suffered grievous injuries and immediately deceased was shifted to nearby hospital for first aid treatment and due to severe injuries sustained by the deceased for further SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 Lakshmamma vs Mohammed Suhail.G on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165502780/
3 management referred to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein, even after better and expert treatment to save the life, Anjinappa H.K. succumbed to fatal injuries and died on the same day at 5.30 p.m.

It is further stated that prior to the date of accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was earning his livelihood as an agriculturiestcumSericulturist and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month and with the said earning, deceased was maintaining his family members.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, petitioners' life has become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.30 lakhs from the respondents.
3. Inspite of due service of notice to the respondents, respondent No.2 and 3 remained absent and placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 appeared before this Tribunal.

The respondent No.1 filed written statement wherein he denies the mode and occurrence of the alleged accident and also alleged involvement of vehicle bearing No.KA04MK5988 as mentioned SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 in the claim petition and further contended that petitioner No.1 is depending on her children.
The petitioner No.2, 4, 5 and 8 are married daughters of deceased and petitioner No.3, 6 and 7 are all married sons and nobody was depending on the deceased.
It is further submitted that as on the date of the alleged accident, respondent No.1 was not the owner of the vehicle bearing No.KA04MK5988 and one Prasanna M. was the owner of the said vehicle.
Hence respondent No.1 prays to dismissal of the claim petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives of the deceased?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that Anjinappa H.K. died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 17.09.2018 at about 9.30 p.m., in between Devanahalli to Gambiranahalli, Sidhaghatta Taluk, Chikkaballapur Talik arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Wagon Car bearing Reg.No.KA04MK 5988?
SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award ?
5. The Petitioner No.6 examined himself as PW.1.
Exs.P1 to 45 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondent No.1 examined himself as RW1 and got marked ExR.1.

4
6. Arguments were addressed on both side.
7. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

sentences.text: The evidence on record reveals that one Muniraju S/o. Anjinappa petitioner No.6 has lodged the complaint after the accident before Shidlaghatta police station, which has been registered by the Shidlaghatta police station in FIR No.284/2018 as per ExP.1.

Thereafter the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet as per ExP.5 against Sandeep.M driver of the offending vehicle and SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 against the respondent No.2 owner of the Wagon R car bearing No.KA04MK5988 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338, 304A of IPC and Sec.196 of IMV Act by holding that on 15.09.2018 at 9.30 p.m., when deceased H.A Anjinappa was returning from the marriage from Hospete along with his friends Narayanappa and Bharathkumar in his Omni car bearing No.KA40M1885 in the KolarChikkaballapura road at that time, the deceased Anjinappa was driving teh Omni car at the left side of the road.

At that time in the KolarChikkaballapura road near Gambiranahalli village in front of Milk Producers Co operative Society, driver of the Wagon R car bearing Reg.No.KA 04MK5988 came from Devanahalli in the opposite direction in high speed and negligent manner and hit to the Maruthi Omni car due to the impact Anjinappa driver of the Omni car sustained grievous injuries and he was succumbed to the injuries on 16.09.2018 at about 5.30 p.m.

5 10.

Apart from this, on perusal of Ex.P.3sketch, Ex.P.2 spot mahazar, it clearly shows that the spot of accident is SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 Chikkaballapura main road and the accident has been taken place on the left side of the road proceeding towards Chikkaballapura.

Admittedly the deceased was driving the vehicle towards the Chikkaballapura and the driver of the offending vehicle was coming from the Chikkaballapura and the accident has been taken place on the left side of the road towards Chikkaballapura.
This clearly establishes that the accident has been taken place as the driver of the offending vehicle drove his vehicle extreme right side of the road and hit to the Omni car driven by the deceased.

Ex.P.4 motor vehicle report and Ex.P.31 to 35 photos clearly shows the severance of the accident and speed of the offending vehicle.
11.
Apart from this, respondent No.1 though examined himself as RW.1 but, has not adduced the evidence of driver of the offending vehicle to prove their contention.

Even the respondent No.1 though contended in his objections that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligence of the deceased but has not lead any evidence of eye witness or the SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 driver of the offending vehicle on his behalf to prove the same.
Apart from this respondent No.1 has not challenged the police documents and the charge sheet filed by the petitioners.

Even though PW.1 was crossexamined at length, but, nothing was elicited from the mouth of the PW.1.
12.
Even either respondent No.1 or other respondents have not challenged and disputed the sketch ExP3.

It is for the respondent No.2 driver of the offending car to state about the facts and circumstances to how the accident has been taken place and why he has drove his car towards right side of the road.
The very silence of the respondent No.2 clearly shows the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving by the respondent No.2 of the offending vehicle.
The evidence of the PW1 coupled with the documents clearly shows involvement of the offending car in the accident.
The respondent No.1 failed to prove that the offending vehicle has not involved in the accident.

There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 collusive.
13.
Apart from this, on perusal of IMV report marked at ExP4, it reveals that on that day the accident has not caused due to any mechanical defect of the above said vehicles.
All these documents clearly shows that due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car and in the said accident Anjinappa H.K. sustained grievous injuries and died.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of driver of the car bearing reg.No.KA04MK5988 and in the said accident Anjinappa H.K. sustained grievous injuries and died.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.1 :

The petitioner No.6 filed affidavit in lieu of his chiefexamination and deposed that he is the son, petitioner No.1 is his mother, petitioner No.2, 4, 5 and 8 are sisters and petitioner No.3 and 7 are his brothers.
The SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 petitioners have produced ExP18 to 26Aadhaar cards of Anjinappa and petitioners.

ExP38 voter ID card, ExP39DL of Anjinappa,
ExP40Adhar card, ExP41pan card and ExP42 genealogical tree.
The said documents reveals is the aforesaid relationship of the claimants with the deceased.

Be that as it may, since the evidence Lakshmamma vs Mohammed Suhail.G on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165502780/
6 led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.

sentences.text: But, respondent No.1 has seriously disputed that petitioner No.2, 4, 6 and 8 daughters married and residing in their matrimonial house and are not dependent on the deceased and hence, they are not entitled for compensation.
In this regard on perusal of the cause title of the petition it reveals that petitioner No.2, 4, 5 and 8 are the married and major and are residing in their matrimonial houses.
Even PW.1 in the crossexamination admitted that petitioner No.2, 4, 5 and 8 are married and are residing in their matrimonial houses.
Hence, it is clear that petitioner No.2, 4, 5 SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 and 8 are not dependent on the deceased.
Hence, petitioner No.2, 4, 5 and 8 are only entitled for the compensation under the conservative heads.
Hence issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
15. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:
From ExP18 Aadhaar card, it reveals that Anjinappa's date of birth is 1948 and as on the date of accident, Anjinappa was aged 70 years.

Admittedly the deceased was married and the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '5'.
16.
According to PW.1, the deceased was doing agriculturist cum sericulurist work and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m. and contributing the entire income for maintaining the family members.
The petitioner No.1 has produced ExP3712 RTCs.
From the said ExP37 RTCs we cannot ascertain the income of the deceased.
Though petitioner has produced Ex.P.14 which shows that from the year 2011 to 2014 deceased was serving as a member of the Hospete Grama Panchayath.
SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019

Further Ex.P.15 shows that deceased was nominated as director of the administrative board of          from 1992 to 1999 and Ex.P.16 shows that deceased was director of the Milk producers Cooperative Society.
Nevertheless they are honorary posts and from Ex.P.14 to 16 this court cannot ascertain any income from these honorary posts.
17. In the absence of proof, this court has to consider the income notionally for calculating the compensation.

As the accident took place in the year 2018 and since the deceased was a semi skilled worker, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,500/ p.m. Needless to mention, also taking into consideration the age of the deceased, nature of his work as well as the present cost of living.
18.
The deceased was married and having four dependents.
Hence 1/4th of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/4th of Rs.12,500/ works out to Rs.3,125/.
Income for consideration is Rs.9,375/ SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 (12,500 - 3,125).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,12,500/ (9,375 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '5'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.5,62,500/ (1,12,500 X 5).
19. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/ (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of loss of spousal Lakshmamma vs Mohammed Suhail.G on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165502780/
7 consortium, parental consortium and loss of love & affection.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner No.1 to 8 being wife, sons and daughters are entitled to the consortium of Rs.48,400/ each.
20. LOSS OF ESTATE:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
21. FUNERAL EXPENSES:

Petitioners are entitled for SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017)
towards funeral expenses.
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioners have produced Ex.P.12 medical bills for Rs.77,153/ for the treatment of deceased Anjinappa before his death.
Hence, an amount of Rs.77,153/ is granted under the head medical expenses.

23. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : Rs.5,62,50000 2 Loss of Consortium : Rs.3,87,20000 3 Loss of Estate : Rs.18,15000 4 Funeral Expenses : Rs.18,15000 5
Medical Expenses : Rs.77,15300 Total Rs.10,63,153=00

Hence, petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.10,63,153=00.
24.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:

Admittedly there is no insurance in the present case and as such, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 with regard to the ownership of the offending vehicle, respondent No.1 lateron by way of amendment to his written statement contended that as on the date of the accident the respondent No.1 was not the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA04MK5988 and Prasanna.D.M was the owner of the said vehicle and even impleaded the said Prasanna D.M as respondent No.3.
In spite of the service of the notice, respondent No.3 has not appeared before the court and contested the case.
Hence, respondent No.3 was placed exparte.

Respondent No.1 examined himself as RW.1 and contended that as on the date of the accident he was not the owner of the offending vehicle and one Prasanna D.M. was the owner of the said vehicle and produced B Extract of the offending vehicle Ex.R.1, which clearly shows that the respondent No.3 was the previous owner and he has sold and transferred the vehicle in the name of the respondent No.1 on 26.09.2018.
Thus, it is clear that till 26.09.2018, Prasanna D.M. was the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA04MK5988.
Admittedly SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 the accident has took place on 15.09.2018.

Thus, it is clear that as on the date of accident i.e., on 15.09.2018,
respondent No.3 was the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA04MK5988.
Admittedly in the present case, there is no insurance to the offending vehicle and police have filed charge sheet U/Sec.196 of the IMV Act.
25. Though police have filed charge sheet against the respondent No.1 as the owner of the vehicle but, charge sheet is not a conclusive proof.
On the other hand, Ex.R.1BExtract clearly shows that as on the date of the accident respondent No.3 was the owner of the vehicle.
Moreover respondent No.3 has not appeared before the court and contested the case.

Though petitioners seriously Lakshmamma vs Mohammed Suhail.G on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165502780/
8 disputed that respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle, crossexamined RW.1 at length and got confronted the indemnity bond of the respondent No.1 as per Ex.P.43 through which he has got released the vehicle and the order sheet in the said case as Ex.P.44 and the charge sheet as per Ex.P.45 but, respondent No.1 being the SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 owner after 26.09.2018 have admittedly got release the vehicle by executing the indemnity bond as per Ex.P.44.
Mere on that basis, it cannot be concluded that respondent No.1 is the R.C. owner of the vehicle as on the date of the accident.
26. Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

27. Therefore, the respondent No.3 being the RC owner is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.3 being the owner of the offending vehicle is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
28. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the findings given on issues SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
: ORDER :
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners No.1, 3, 6 and 7 are entitled for the compensation of Rs.6,75,953/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

The petitioners No.1 to 8 are equally entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,87,200/ (consortium)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.3 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit together with interest, out of the compensation amount Rs.6,75,953/ the petitioner No.1, 3, 6 & 7 are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows:
 Petitioner No.1 55  %
 SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019  Petitioner No.3 15  %
 Petitioner No.6 15  %
 Petitioner No.7 15  %
The entire amount of Petitioner No.1 to 8 shall be released to them through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 to 8 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a petition filed under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Anjinappa in a road traffic accident.
claiming for compensation of with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
Admittedly the deceased was driving the vehicle towards the Chikkaballapura and the driver of the offending vehicle was coming from the Chikkaballapura and the accident has been taken place on the left side of the road towards Chikkaballapura.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives of the deceased?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that Anjinappa H.K. died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 17.09.2018 at about 9.30 p.m., in between Devanahalli to Gambiranahalli, Sidhaghatta Taluk, Chikkaballapur Talik arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Wagon Car bearing Reg.No.KA04MK 5988?
SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thereafter the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet as per ExP.5 against Sandeep.M driver of the offending vehicle and SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 against the respondent No.2 owner of the Wagon R car bearing No.KA04MK5988 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338, 304A of IPC and Sec.196 of IMV Act by holding that on 15.09.2018 at 9.30 p.m., when deceased H.A Anjinappa was returning from the marriage from Hospete along with his friends Narayanappa and Bharathkumar in his Omni car bearing No.KA40M1885 in the KolarChikkaballapura road at that time, the deceased Anjinappa was driving teh Omni car at the left side of the road.
It is for the respondent No.2 driver of the offending car to state about the facts and circumstances to how the accident has been taken place and why he has drove his car towards right side of the road.
The very silence of the respondent No.2 clearly shows the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving by the respondent No.2 of the offending vehicle.
The evidence of the PW1 coupled with the documents clearly shows involvement of the offending car in the accident.
The respondent No.1 failed to prove that the offending vehicle has not involved in the accident.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 collusive.
13.
Apart from this, on perusal of IMV report marked at ExP4, it reveals that on that day the accident has not caused due to any mechanical defect of the above said vehicles.
17. In the absence of proof, this court has to consider the income notionally for calculating the compensation.
As the accident took place in the year 2018 and since the deceased was a semi skilled worker, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,500/ p.m. Needless to mention, also taking into consideration the age of the deceased, nature of his work as well as the present cost of living.
18.
Hence, respondent No.3 was placed exparte.
Thus, it is clear that till 26.09.2018, Prasanna D.M. was the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA04MK5988.
Thus, it is clear that as on the date of accident i.e., on 15.09.2018,
respondent No.3 was the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA04MK5988.
Admittedly in the present case, there is no insurance to the offending vehicle and police have filed charge sheet U/Sec.196 of the IMV Act.
25. Though police have filed charge sheet against the respondent No.1 as the owner of the vehicle but, charge sheet is not a conclusive proof.
On the other hand, Ex.R.1BExtract clearly shows that as on the date of the accident respondent No.3 was the owner of the vehicle.
Mere on that basis, it cannot be concluded that respondent No.1 is the R.C. owner of the vehicle as on the date of the accident.
26. Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Petitioner No.1 to 8 being wife, sons and daughters are entitled to the consortium of Rs.48,400/ each.
20. LOSS OF ESTATE:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
27. Therefore, the respondent No.3 being the RC owner is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
28. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the findings given on issues SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019 No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
: ORDER :
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners No.1, 3, 6 and 7 are entitled for the compensation of Rs.6,75,953/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The petitioners No.1 to 8 are equally entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,87,200/ (consortium)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.3 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit together with interest, out of the compensation amount Rs.6,75,953/ the petitioner No.1, 3, 6 & 7 are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows:
 Petitioner No.1 55  %
 SCCH-6 MVC No.271/2019  Petitioner No.3 15  %
 Petitioner No.6 15  %
 Petitioner No.7 15  %
The entire amount of Petitioner No.1 to 8 shall be released to them through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 to 8 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.
